title: wg: soften protocol-07 §4.1's mutual-TLS MUST, standalone (drafted, hold for Mark)
description:
Drafted 2026-11-26 and HELD. Do not send without Mark's OK (memory:
dont-flood-upstream).

The highest value per word of anything in the personal drafts (bead
mimid-1wgh.37.15): it unblocks every implementation that does not do
mTLS, needs no new mechanism, and does not depend on
draft-atwood-mimi-provider-auth being adopted.

## Why provider-auth's existing text cannot be sent as-is

provider-auth §"Replacement Text for the MIMI Protocol" already
proposes this change, but its text reads "using one of the mechanisms in
[this document]" and "Every provider implements the DNS key mechanism of
[this document], Section 5". So it only works if provider-auth is
adopted. The point of sending it standalone is to remove a counterfactual
mandate NOW, without asking the WG for anything else, so the text has to
stand alone. That is what is drafted below.

## The three places, exact text in -07

1. §2, txt line 303: "The MIMI transport is based on HTTPS over
   mutually-authenticated TLS."
2. §4.1, txt lines 981-984: "The TLS connection underlying the HTTPS
   connection MUST be mutually authenticated.  The certificates
   presented in the TLS handshake MUST authenticate the source and
   target provider domains, according to [RFC6125]."
3. §9, txt line 3376: "Individual protocol actions are protected against
   network attackers with mutually-authenticated TLS, where the TLS
   certificates authenticate the identities that the protocol actors
   assert at the application layer."

Also: [RFC6125] is obsoleted by [RFC9525]. That is a free erratum and
could go as its own one-line issue so nothing holds it up.

## PROPOSED ISSUE TEXT (short, as WG issues should be)

> Title: §4.1's mutual-TLS MUST does not describe deployed
> implementations
>
> §4.1 requires that "The TLS connection underlying the HTTPS
> connection MUST be mutually authenticated", with certificates
> authenticating both provider domains.
>
> Two implementations do not do this. One authenticates every operation
> except the directory with RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures and
> presents no TLS client certificate at all. The other implements
> client certificates but has never completed a mutually authenticated
> handshake with a peer; its interop runs on signatures.
>
> There is also a structural reason it is unlikely to be met: the Web
> PKI does not issue client certificates for federation at scale, so a
> provider that wants one needs a private arrangement with each peer.
>
> We suggest keeping the security requirement and dropping the
> single-mechanism mandate. For §4.1:
>
>   The TLS connection underlying the HTTPS connection MUST
>   authenticate the target provider's domain, according to [RFC9525].
>
>   The target provider MUST authenticate the source provider's domain
>   name, which is the identity the rest of this document relies on.
>   Mutually authenticated TLS, in which the certificate presented by
>   the source provider authenticates its domain according to
>   [RFC9525], satisfies this requirement. Which mechanisms a target
>   provider accepts is a matter of local policy, and a source and a
>   target provider MAY use any mechanism they have agreed on that
>   authenticates the source provider's domain name.
>
> For §2: "The MIMI transport is based on HTTPS. The target provider is
> authenticated by TLS; the source provider is authenticated as
> described in Section 4.1."
>
> For §9: "Individual protocol actions are protected against network
> attackers by TLS, and the source provider is authenticated to the
> target as described in Section 4.1, so that the identity a protocol
> actor asserts at the application layer is the one that was
> authenticated."
>
> Note that [RFC6125], cited in §4.1, is obsoleted by [RFC9525].
>
> This is a loosening, and it leaves a gap: two providers could each
> conform and still fail to interoperate, one accepting only signatures
> and the other offering only certificates. Closing that needs a
> mandatory-to-implement mechanism, which we think the WG will want to
> choose separately. We would rather the document described a property
> implementations meet, and then chose a common mechanism, than keep a
> mandate that current deployments do not follow.

## The honest cost, for our own notes

This IS weaker in conformance terms: a MUST naming one well-understood
mechanism becomes a MUST naming a property. The "both conform, neither
interoperates" objection is real and a reviewer will raise it, so the
issue text raises it first rather than being caught by it.

The answer is a mandatory-to-implement mechanism, which is what
provider-auth proposes (DNS keys, mandatory to implement). Sending the
softening first and the mechanism second is deliberate: it separates
"the current text is counterfactual", which is hard to argue with, from
"here is my mechanism", which is a bigger ask.

## Evidence

- coland: bead mimid-1wgh.46.11.2. No TLS client certificates at all;
  RFC 9421 signatures on every operation but the directory.
- mimid: both halves implemented, never deployed or tested with a peer
  (AGENTS.md is explicit that we must not claim conformance). Epic
  mimid-75nk, decision mimid-75nk.14 on why we present a certificate
  only to peers configured to trust it.
- provider-auth §"The Web PKI Has Left the Federation" carries the
  structural argument; §"Precedent: How Email Federates" the analogy.

Name no implementation but ours without checking first whether the
deviation is our own bug (bead mimid-7yn7.9) -- the issue text above
says "one implementation" rather than naming coland, deliberately.

## Status: HELD, Mark 2026-11-26

Asked and answered: keep holding, decide later. The text is ready and
is not to be sent. Nothing rides along with it either, so the small
uncontroversial sends stay held too (the RFC 6125 -> RFC 9525 erratum,
the accepted -> success PR on branch submit-response-success, the
GroupInfoCode reserved(0) question, and the directory-member registry
ask). None of them is time-sensitive.

Do not raise this again unprompted.
close_reason: Sent 2026-11-26 as ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-protocol issue 229. Named mimid for its own half and left the other implementation anonymous (bead mimid-7yn7.9); no JMAP in it (AGENTS.md); the issue raises the interop gap against itself and points at a mandatory-to-implement mechanism as a separate WG decision, so it is not an argument for provider-auth.
